title: The Famous Potter Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Conan, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. The 'Fusui-maru' that Masuko breaks is itself a counterfeit Seto secretly made and swapped in -- the real Fusui-maru is stored elsewhere -- which is why Seto shrugs off its destruction ('that thing can turn to dust for all I care'). Two pupils (Seto and Otani) each briefly left the stateroom that morning, giving genuine structural red herring material before the blood-spatter and lipstick evidence isolates Seto specifically. case_type: murder.

objects.name: Protruding nail on the storeroom shelf

attrs.significance: cut Masuko's calf as she lost her balance and fell -- an unplanned injury that produced a blood-spatter pattern inconsistent with the 'carried by arms and legs' story and pointed to her having been up on the shelf

clues.desc: Blood drops found near the shelf show a splatter pattern consistent with falling more than a meter, but if Masuko's body had only been carried at floor level by her arms and legs (as the pupils claimed), the fall to the floor would be at most 50cm -- proving she had been up on the shelf, not just carried afterward.

Whoever called Masuko's phone that morning reported 'she's not answering' -- but her phone was later found turned off, and a genuinely off phone returns an out-of-service message, not silence. That mismatch means the caller actually dialed a different number: the one hidden in the pot.

A lipstick smear turns up on the back of Seto's jacket and on a stateroom cushion, matching the mark left where Masuko's body was found -- consistent with her having been carried over his shoulder up a ladder, not merely lifted by arms and legs after the fact.
